title: env.sandbox.timeline.export request
description: Run a timeline exactly as `env.sandbox.timeline` does, then write each step's checkpointed ranges as files under the step's own name. `prepared_output`: accepts only `prepare` and `commit_reviewed`. The read-only operation reports a digest per checkpoint and no bytes, which is right for a response — sixty ticks each checkpointing a framebuffer is one nobody can read — and leaves no way to *get* the bytes at all: re-running the interesting step through `env.sandbox.call` only works when the step can be reproduced as a standalone call, and a step deep in an evolving timeline cannot, because its inputs are the machine every step before it produced. Nothing is written until every step has run.

hunk.description: Which CODE hunk to run. Defaults to the first.

load_origin.description: Absolute address the selected hunk is mapped at.

entry_offset.description: Byte offset within the hunk to start at.

hunk_bases.description: Additional hunks to map, for relocations that target them. A hunk relocated into but not mapped is an error, not a silent skip: the code would run with an address that means nothing and the trace would not say so.

maximum_steps.description: Instructions to execute before stopping. Clamped to what the executing context allows — 200000 by default, and at most 50000000 for a host running local media it has reviewed. Sandbox code is unknown code, and a request for an unbounded run would be asking the process to hang, so the budget is always finite. A reduction is reported as LIMIT_REDUCED.

watch.description: Absolute ranges whose accesses are attached to trace rows. At most 64: every watched range is compared against every memory access, so the list is a per-access cost rather than a per-request one. An excess is refused rather than truncated, because a dropped watchpoint would make a run that observed nothing indistinguishable from one that had nothing to observe.

stop_on_watch.description: Stop at the first instruction that touches a watched range.

trace.description: Whether to return the per-instruction trace. Watching implies recording even without this, or a watch hit would stop the run with nothing to point at.

stack_arguments.description: Longwords placed above the return marker: at entry SP holds the marker and SP+4 is the first argument, as a JSR would leave them.

mapped_regions.description: Regions the routine reads or writes, beyond the hunks it runs in.

interrupts.description: Interrupts delivered on a deterministic instruction schedule. Setup code commonly sets a synchronization flag and spins until an interrupt handler clears it; the beam counter advances on its own, but nothing runs the handler, so otherwise valid initialization never returns. The schedule is in instructions rather than in beam or wall-clock time because that is the one clock a sandbox reproduces exactly.

memory_exports.description: Ranges of the memory the whole timeline leaves behind, each under a name. A step's own `checkpoints` are the same thing recorded as that step left it. The result digests each range; a range that is not mapped refuses the timeline before any step runs.

memory_seeds.description: Bytes written into the sandbox before entry. Each seed spells its bytes out as `hex`, copies them from a range with `from`, or replays them from a pinned `artifact` — exactly one of the three, since a seed with two would have two answers to what it seeds and one with none would seed nothing while looking like it seeded something.

maximum_total_steps.description: Instructions the whole timeline may execute. Separate from a step's own budget and not its multiple: a step is never clipped to what is left, it either runs with the budget it asked for or is reported as not run. Defaults to one run's budget, which is deliberately conservative.

steps.description: The steps, in the order they run and are reported. Each one either enters a routine with `entry_offset` or continues the previous step's machine with `resume`. Once a step is refused or does not run, no step after it runs either: the order is the experiment, and a later step continuing a machine that skipped its predecessor would be a different timeline reported under this one's name.

name.description: Unique within the timeline, and usable as one path component. Uniqueness is what lets a result be matched to a step by something other than its position.

entry_offset.description: Enter this hunk offset as a fresh call, with the return marker below the stated arguments. Exactly one of this and `resume`.

resume.description: Continue the machine the previous step left, from the address it stopped at and with the register file it left behind. The first step cannot resume: there is no machine to continue. Neither can a step whose predecessor's routine returned — the machine is then sitting on the return marker with nothing left to continue.

data_registers.description: D0-D7 at entry, defaulting to the shared recipe's. Only for a step that enters: a resumed step continues with the registers it stopped with, and replacing part of that machine's state would build one no execution produced.

address_registers.description: A0-A6 at entry, on the same terms as data_registers.

stack_arguments.description: Replaces the shared stack arguments outright rather than appending: a call's arguments are positional, and appending would shift them. Only for a step that enters.

memory_seeds.description: Bytes written into the machine before this step runs — the reviewed input change a tick consumes. They are applied before the step's own baseline is taken, so what the step reports as changed memory is what its execution did, and the seeds are reported beside it as the inputs they are.

maximum_steps.description: Instructions this step may execute, defaulting to the shared budget and clamped by the same context ceiling. A step is never clipped to what the aggregate budget has left: it either runs with the budget it asked for or is reported as not run.

stop_at.description: Absolute addresses to stop at, before the instruction there executes. A breakpoint at the address the step starts from does not stop it before it has executed anything; otherwise a step resuming at its own breakpoint could never make progress. The suppression lasts only while the program counter is still there, so a loop that comes back does stop.

checkpoints.description: Ranges of memory recorded as this step left them, each under a name. The result carries a digest per range rather than the bytes: a timeline of sixty ticks each checkpointing a framebuffer is a response nobody can read, and `env.sandbox.call.export` on the same recipe is what produces the bytes when one of them turns out to matter. A range that is not mapped refuses the whole timeline before any step runs.

length.description: At least one byte: a zero-length range would write an empty file that looks like a successful export.

name.description: What the range is called, as a file name. A single component: the destination names the directory, and a name that could contain a separator would be deciding a second one.

notes.description: What this step is for, in the record. Never interpreted.

destination.description: Directory the golden record goes in, as an identity the adapter resolves against its own output root.

file_name.description: What the aggregate result is written as. The per-step files are named `<step>/<checkpoint>` beside it, and the manifest is named from this. Defaults to timeline.json.
